children: Ninety-one per cent of the city’s passenger traffic will remain unaffected as Mumbai International Airport Limited undertakes partial redevelopment of Terminal 1 from January 2027, Adani Airports Holdings Limited (AAHL) chief executive officer Arun Bansal said in a statement on Saturday evening.

“Ninety-one per cent of Mumbai airport’s passenger traffic will remain unaffected even as we undertake redevelopment of the age-old infrastructure that was in urgent need of repairs. Only the north section of Terminal 1B, which accounts for around one-third of Terminal 1’s capacity, is being demolished in Phase 1 to minimise passenger inconvenience and operational disruption. The transition to Navi Mumbai Airport is temporary and does not represent a permanent shift of Mumbai Airport traffic,” Bansal said.

To ensure continuity of operations and minimise inconvenience to passengers, the Adani group has provided airlines with the option to temporarily relocate their operations to Navi Mumbai International Airport at their discretion.
“ AAHL will support airlines through this transition and will provide all necessary assistance to ensure a smooth and seamless migration of services,” it said
The airport operator has proposed that one-third of international flights shift to Navi Mumbai from October 26, but airlines are resisting the plan, calling it a forced relocation.

title: Mumbai airport Terminal 1 revamp: 91% passenger traffic to remain unaffected
